extracted.intended_audience: advocacy organizations, campaign staff, and practitioners considering whether and how to submit public comments on agency climate rulemaking (especially EPA actions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for advocacy organizations on whether to file public comments and how to position those comments in response to the EPA's proposed rescission of the 2009 endangerment finding. Emphasizes strategic timing, framing, and resource prioritization for groups that typically focus on Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — comment when agency action defines statutory baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: File targeted comments at moments of legal exposure (e.g., when an agency action will define the future statutory baseline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor agency rulemaking that can change the legal baseline; prioritize filing comments during those windows even if agency work is not your organization's main focus. Example: CCL filed on the EPA proposal because it could redefine the baseline for federal climate regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — use comments as a defensive backstop, not the primary lever
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive regulations are fragile and shift with administrations; comments can be filed as a defensive backstop rather than the primary strategy for achieving durable policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate most resources to pursuing durable, congressionally-enacted solutions, but maintain capacity to submit comments to defend existing legal foundations when threatened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive framing — argue statutory misinterpretation and congressional intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenge the agency's legal reading by arguing the EPA has misinterpreted the Clean Air Act and congressional intent (e.g., citing 'Congress' decadeslong support for the EPA's mandate to regulate greenhouse gas emissions').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground comments in statutory interpretation and legislative history; reference concrete legislative actions that demonstrate congressional backing (the post cites the Inflation Reduction Act as an example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience fit — file comments when your voice can meaningfully contribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations with a primarily legislative theory of change can still file targeted comments when their voice and perspective will add meaningful value to the administrative record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether your organization's credibility, expertise, or constituency offers a distinct perspective that could influence the agency or the public record before deciding to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical process — submit formal, timely comments and track deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comment processes have explicit windows and deadlines (the EPA comment period in this case was open until Sept 15, 2025; EPA received over 44,000 comments within the first week).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure formal submission procedures are followed and calendar deadlines are tracked; be prepared for high comment volume and the need for clear, concise submissions to stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic prioritization — balance long-term legislative strategy with short-term administrative defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize long-term, durable solutions (congressional action) while recognizing moments where short-term administrative engagement is necessary to prevent regressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal strategy criteria to decide when to divert limited staff/time to rulemaking comments versus legislative lobbying; document that comments are tactical, not a shift in overall strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Messaging — emphasize legislative backing to counter agency rescission
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame arguments to show that Congress has supported the agency's mandate over decades, undermining claims to rescind foundational findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit examples of congressional support (statutes, appropriations, major legislation) in comment text to bolster claims about congressional intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational decision rule — treat agency comments as opportunistic interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: See filing comments as an opportunity to intervene opportunistically when legal exposure threatens policy, even for groups that usually focus elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a decision rule in organizational strategy: maintain openness to targeted administrative engagement when the stakes and potential impact justify the effort.
